prompt: Write a recorded statement transcript (about 250 words) between an insurance adjuster (lines start with 'Q:') and the claimant (lines start with 'A:'). The claimant was the driver in a hit while turning left in Houston, Texas, and has back strain. No names, no dates. (Internal reference C-1030; do not mention it.)
text:
Q: Thank you for agreeing to give this recorded statement. Please state your full name for the record.

A: I'd rather not give my name on a recording, but you can use the claim file reference.

Q: That's fine. Can you tell me where you were when the collision happened?

A: I was in Houston, Texas, at an intersection near a shopping center. I was driving my sedan and turning left across the lanes of oncoming traffic.

Q: What was the traffic signal doing when you started your turn?

A: The light had turned yellow when I entered the intersection. I thought I had time to clear it, and I was looking for a gap in the oncoming cars.

Q: Did you see the other vehicle before impact?

A: Not really. I saw headlights, but I didn't judge its speed well. It came through and hit the driver's side of my car.

Q: Were you injured?

A: Yes. My lower back hurt right away, and by the next morning it was stiff and sore. I've been seeing a doctor who diagnosed a back strain, and I'm doing physical therapy twice a week.

Q: Are you still having trouble with your back?

A: Yes. Sitting for long periods and lifting anything heavy makes it worse. I've had to miss some work because of it.

Q: Did you speak with anyone at the scene?

A: I gave a short statement to the other driver and to the officer who responded. The officer wrote up a report.

Q: Is there anything else you want to add?

A: Only that I'm willing to cooperate fully and provide my medical records once you send the authorization form.

Q: Thank you. That concludes the statement.
